author: Sylvia Plath
description: The 20 most representative poems of Sylvia Plath

poems.title: Daddy
poems.text:
You do not do, you do not do
Any more, black shoe
In which I have lived like a foot
For thirty years, poor and white,
Barely daring to breathe or Achoo.

Daddy, I have had to kill you.
You died before I had time——
Marble-heavy, a bag full of God,
Ghastly statue with one gray toe
Big as a Frisco seal

And a head in the freakish Atlantic
Where it pours bean green over blue
In the waters off beautiful Nauset.
I used to pray to recover you.
Ach, du.

In the German tongue, in the Polish town
Scraped flat by the roller
Of wars, wars, wars.
But the name of the town is common.
My Polack friend

Says there are a dozen or two.
So I never could tell where you
Put your foot, your root,
I never could talk to you.
The tongue stuck in my jaw.

It stuck in a barb wire snare.
Ich, ich, ich, ich,
I could hardly speak.
I thought every German was you.
And the language obscene

An engine, an engine
Chuffing me off like a Jew.
A Jew to Dachau, Auschwitz, Belsen.
I began to talk like a Jew.
I think I may well be a Jew.

The snows of the Tyrol, the clear beer of Vienna
Are not very pure or true.
With my gypsy ancestress and my weird luck
And my Taroc pack and my Taroc pack
I may be a bit of a Jew.

I have always been scared of you,
With your Luftwaffe, your gobbledygoo.
And your neat mustache
And your Aryan eye, bright blue.
Panzer-man, panzer-man, O You——

Not God but a swastika
So black no sky could squeak through.
Every woman adores a Fascist,
The boot in the face, the brute
Brute heart of a brute like you.

You stand at the blackboard, daddy,
In the picture I have of you,
A cleft in your chin instead of your foot
But no less a devil for that, no not
Any less the black man who

Bit my pretty red heart in two.
I was twenty when they killed you.
I was thirty.
Dear God, how I wished I could remember you.
But the tongue stuck in my jaw.

It stuck in a barb wire snare.
Ich, ich, ich, ich,
I could hardly speak.
I thought every German was you.
And the language obscene

An engine, an engine
Chuffing me off like a Jew.
A Jew to Dachau, Auschwitz, Belsen.
I began to talk like a Jew.
I think I may well be a Jew.

I have always been scared of you,
With your Luftwaffe, your gobbledygoo.
And your neat mustache
And your Aryan eye, bright blue.
Panzer-man, panzer-man, O You——

There's a stake in your fat black heart
And the villagers never liked you.
They are dancing and stamping on you.
They always knew it was you.
Daddy, daddy, you bastard, I'm through.

poems.title: Lady Lazarus
poems.text:
I have done it again.
One year in every ten
I manage it——

A sort of walking miracle, my skin
Bright as a Nazi lampshade,
My right foot

A paperweight,
My face a featureless, fine
Jew linen.

Peel off the napkin
O enemy.
Do I terrify?——

The nose, the eye pits, the full set of teeth?
The sour breath
Will vanish in a day.

Soon, soon the flesh
The grave cave ate will be at
Home on me

And I a smiling woman.
I am only thirty.
And like the cat I have nine times to die.

This is Number Three.
What a trash
To annihilate each decade.

What a million filaments.
The peanut-crunching crowd
Shoves in to see

Them unwrap me hand and foot——
The big strip tease.
Gentlemen, ladies

These are my hands,
My knees.
I may be skin and bone.

Nevertheless, I am the same, identical woman.
The first time it happened I was ten.
It was an accident.

The second time I meant
To last it out and not come back at all.
I rocked shut

As a seashell.
They had to call and call
And pick the worms off me like sticky pearls.

Dying
Is an art, like everything else.
I do it exceptionally well.

I do it so it feels like hell.
I do it so it feels real.
I guess you could say I've a call.

It's easy enough to do it in a cell.
It's easy enough to do it and stay put.
It's the theatrical

Comeback in broad day
To the same place, the same face, the same brute
Amused shout:

'A miracle!'That knocks me out.
There is a charge

For the eyeing of my scars, there is a charge
For the hearing of my heart——
It really goes.

And there is a charge, a very large charge
For a word or a touch
Or a bit of blood

Or a piece of my hair or my clothes.
So, so, Herr Doktor.
So, Herr Enemy.

I am your ops,
I am your treasure,
One fine day

The peanut-crunching crowd
Shoves in to see
Them unwrap me hand and foot——

The big strip tease.
Gentlemen, ladies

These are my hands,
My knees.
I may be skin and bone.

Nevertheless, I am the same, identical woman.
First time it happened I was ten.
It was an accident.

Second time I meant
To last it out and not come back at all.
I rocked shut

As a seashell.
They had to call and call
And pick the worms off me like sticky pearls.

Dying
Is an art, like everything else.
I do it exceptionally well.

I do it so it feels like hell.
I do it so it feels real.
I guess you could say I've a call.

It's easy enough to do it in a cell.
It's easy enough to do it and stay put.
It's the theatrical

Comeback in broad day
To the same place, the same face, the same brute
Amused shout:

'A miracle!'That knocks me out.
There is a charge

For the eyeing of my scars, there is a charge
For the hearing of my heart——
It really goes.

And there is a charge, a very large charge
For a word or a touch
Or a bit of blood

Or a piece of my hair or my clothes.
So, so, Herr Doktor.
So, Herr Enemy.

I am your ops,
I am your treasure.
One fine day

The peanut-crunching crowd
Shoves in to see
Me eating men like air.

Beware
Beware.
Out of the ash
I rise with my red hair
And I eat men like air.

poems.title: Ariel
poems.text:
Stasis in darkness.
Then the substanceless blue
Pour of tor and distances.

God's lioness,
How one we grow,
Pivot of heels and knees!——The furrow
Splits and passes, body into white,
Eye, a row of water.

I am the arrow,
The dew that flies
Suicidal, at one with the drive
Into the red

Eye, the cauldron of morning.

poems.title: Tulips
poems.text:
The tulips are too excitable, it is winter here.
Look how white everything is, how quiet, how snowed-in.
I am learning peacefulness, lying by myself quietly
As the light lies on these white walls, this bed, these hands.
I am nobody; I have nothing to do with explosions.
I have given my name and my day-clothes to the nurses
And my history to the anesthetist and my body to surgeons.

They have propped my head between the pillow and the sheet-cuff
Like an eye between two white lids that will not shut.
It is snowing inside me and I am dissipating.
There is this white wall, and this white light, and this silence.
The nurses move all about with their trays, quiet as doves.
They wear their bright surgical gowns and they are pleasant.
They do not tell me that I am being bled.

I am getting better.
The red tulips are my first flowers.
I did not think you could be so quiet.
I did not think you could be so small.
I did not think you could be so white.
I did not think you could be so alive.

The tulips are too excitable, it is winter here.
I have given my name and my day-clothes to the nurses
And my history to the anesthetist and my body to surgeons.
I am nobody; I have nothing to do with explosions.
I have given my eyes to the oculist, my teeth to the dentist,
And my story to the anesthetist.

I have given my name and my day-clothes to the nurses.
I am nobody; I have nothing to do with explosions.
I have given my heart to the cardiologist.
My teeth to the dentist.
And my eyes to the oculist.

The tulips are too excitable.
I am getting better.

poems.title: Morning Song
poems.text:
Love set you going like a fat gold watch.
The midwife slapped your footsoles, and your bald cry
Took its place among the elements.

Our voices echo, magnifying your arrival.
New statue.
In a drafty museum, your nakedness
Shadows our safety.
We stand round blankly as walls.

I'm no more your mother
Than the cloud that distills a mirror to reflect its own slow
Effacement across the wind.
I'm no more your mother
Than the dew in the morning
That stirs the water of a lake.

I've given you my life.
You have taken it.
You have set it free.
I have given you my life.
You have given me back.

All the same, something about you
Gives me pause.
Your mouth is open as any cat's,
As a baby's.
Your cry is the one thing I hear.

And it's the most human sound I know.
It's the sound of hunger,
The sound of the first thing,
The sound that says I'm here,
I'm here.

poems.title: Mirror
poems.text:
I am silver and exact. I have no preconceptions.
Whatever I see I swallow immediately
Just as it is, unmisted by love or dislike.
I am not cruel, only truthful——
The eye of a little god, four-cornered.

Most of the time I meditate on the opposite wall.
It is pink, with speckles. I have looked at it so long
I think it is a part of my heart. But it flickers.
Faces and darkness separate us over and over.

Now I am a lake. A woman bends over me,
Searching my surface for what she really is.
Then she turns to those liars, the candles or the moon.
I see her back, and reflect it faithfully.
She rewards me with tears and an agitation of hands.

I am important to her. She comes and goes.
In each morning the gray-faced houses,
The coldness of the mirror,
The red, the redness of the water.

poems.title: The Applicant
poems.text:
First, are you our sort of a person?
Do you wear
A glass eye, or false teeth or a crutch,
A brace or a hook,
Rubber breasts or a rubber crotch,

Stitches to show something's missing? No, no?
Then how can we give you a thing?

Stop crying.
Open your hands.
Empty your pocket.
Is it money? Is it a flower?
Is it a stone?

Are you our sort of person?
Do you handle?
What shape is your wound?
Does it open or close?
Do you know how to sew?

We have a new matchless product
Of the finest workmanship.
This product is not sold without a body.

You have a body?
Yes.
Good.

A living doll, everywhere you look.
It can sew, it can cook,
It can talk, talk, talk.
It can walk.

It can do it all.
Believe me, they'll bury you in it.

Do you need a companion?
There is one.

Take her.
She can cook and sew,
She can talk and walk,
She can do it all.

She is a living doll.
Do you need a companion?
Take her.

She can do it all.
She is a living doll.
She is a living doll.
Do you need a companion?
Take her.

Believe me, they'll bury you in it.

poems.title: Poppies in October
poems.text:
Even the sun-clouds this morning cannot manage such skirts.
Nor the woman in the ambulance
Whose red heart blooms through her coat so astoundingly——

A gift, a gift!
Your heart is too pure,
Too red, too lovely,
Too red,
You are too beautiful.

The ambulance, the ambulance,
It has taken everything from me.
I have nothing left.

Even the sun-clouds this morning cannot manage such skirts.
The woman in the ambulance,
Her red heart blooms through her coat.

I do not want to be so pretty.
I do not want the red heart.
I do not want the ambulance.
I do not want to be so beautiful.

I want my eyes back.
I want my heart back.
I want my life back.

poems.title: Edge
poems.text:
The woman is perfected.
Her dead
Body wears the smile of accomplishment,

The illusion of a Greek necessity
Flows in the scrolls of her toga,
Her bare
Feet seem to be saying:

We have come so far, it is over.
Each one closed in on itself,
The secret is sealed.

Each child stretches its cradle.
Each face stands, haggard and gaunt.
All night the dew falls.

The old men sit in their chairs
With their white hair
Streaming down their backs.

The boy
Stands on tiptoe.
His lips are parted.

He has a new coat.
His feet are bare.
He does not move.

The children are gone.
The woman is perfected.
Her dead
Body wears the smile of accomplishment,

The illusion of a Greek necessity
Flows in the scrolls of her toga,
Her bare
Feet seem to be saying:

We have come so far, it is over.
Each one closed in on itself,
The secret is sealed.

poems.title: Elm
poems.text:
I know the bottom, she said. I know it with my great tap root:
It is what you fear.
I do not fear it: I have been there.

Is it the sea you hear in me,
Its dissatisfactions?
Or the voice of nothing, that was your madness?

Love is a shadow.
How you lie and cry after it
Listen: these are its feet.

It walks on rain, and walks on rain,
And the moon is its left eye.
It walks on rain,
And the moon is its left eye.

It has the yellow hair of a child.
It is the ghost of a virgin.
It has the dark wood of a forest.

I have been there so many times.
It has killed me, it has killed me.
I am the one it loves.

And you, darling, are the one it wants.
And you, darling, are the one it wants.
And I know the bottom, she said.

poems.title: The Moon and the Yew Tree
poems.text:
This is the light of the mind, cold and planetary.
The trees of the mind are black, the light is blue.
The grasses are overloaded with the moon,
And the bare light of the moon falls through the trees.

The yew tree is black, the light is blue.
The moon is the mother of the yew tree,
The yew tree is the daughter of the moon.
The yew tree is the shadow of the moon.

The grasses are overloaded with the moon.
The moon is a woman, and the yew tree is her daughter.
The moon is a woman, and the yew tree is her daughter.
The moon is a woman, and the yew tree is her daughter.

The light of the mind is cold and planetary.
The trees of the mind are black, the light is blue.
The moon is a woman, and the yew tree is her daughter.

poems.title: Nick and the Candlestick
poems.text:
You are the one
Solid the spaces lean on, envious.
You are the baby in the barn.

O love, how did you get here?
O love, how did you get here?

The coldness of you is staggering,
But I can still touch you.
Your mouth is the size of a pin.

Your mouth is the size of a pin.
O love, how did you get here?

You are the one
Solid the spaces lean on, envious.
You are the baby in the barn.

The candlesticks are lit,
The wax is dripping.
O love, how did you get here?

The night is cold.
The night is cold.
O love, how did you get here?

poems.title: Fever 103°
poems.text:
Pure? What does it mean?
The tongues of hell
Are dull,
Dull as the double
goldén Companions that hang
dumbly over the door——
The gilded snouts
Of Wisdom!

I am too pure for you or anyone.
Your body
Hurts me as the world hurts God.
I am a lantern——
My head a moon
Of orange-paper,

Flimsy of me.
I must
Travel alone.
The souffle of hell
gains.

What is this, anyhow?
The gold of my flesh burns.
The gold of my flesh burns.

I am too pure for you or anyone.
I am too pure to live.
I am too pure to die.

I am too pure for anyone.
The gold of my flesh burns.
The gold of my flesh burns.

I am not a body, I am a soul.
I am not a body, I am a soul.
I am not a body, I am a soul.

The angel of the world,
Dressed in a white robe,
Flies out of my mouth.

poems.title: The Colossus
poems.text:
I shall never get you put together entirely,
Pieced, glued, and properly jointed.
Mule bray, caterpillar grieve.

Stalely aware of the smell of your stone.
I have come to my bones.
No one's experience of you is so complete.

No one's experience of you is so complete.
I shall never get you put together entirely.
Pieced, glued, and properly jointed.

O father, I do not know how I came to you.
I do not know how I came to you.
Mule bray, caterpillar grieve.

Stalely aware of the smell of your stone.
I shall never get you put together entirely.
Pieced, glued, and properly jointed.

I am the girl you ran off with.
I am the girl you did not marry.
Mule bray, caterpillar grieve.

poems.title: Waking in Winter
poems.text:
I like the cool half-dark of winter.
I like the stars.
I like the sound of the wind
In the eaves.

I like the way the night comes down
Like a curtain of black velvet.

I like the moon.
I like the stars.
I like the sound of the wind
In the eaves.

I like the way the snow falls.
I like the way the frost comes.
I like the way the world
Is white and clean.

I like the silence of winter.
I like the way the night
Comes down like a curtain.
I like the stars.

I like the way the wind
Sounds in the chimney.
I like the way the fire
Goes out.

I like the winter.
I like the cold.
I like the way the snow
Falls and falls.

poems.title: Crossing the Water
poems.text:
Black lake, black boat, two black,
Cut paper hearts.

Night, and light, and the moon,
And the white, wet moon.

The white moon,
The white moon,
The white moon.

The lake is black.
The boat is black.
The hearts are black.

Night, and light, and the moon.
The white moon.

I am going,
I am going,
I am going.

poems.title: Insensibility
poems.text:
I am a girl without a face.
I am a girl without eyes.
I am a girl without a mouth.
I am a girl without a body.

I am a girl without a brain.
I am a girl without a soul.
I am a girl without a heart.
I am a girl without a name.

I am a girl without a past.
I am a girl without a future.
I am a girl without a present.
I am a girl without a life.

I am a girl without a death.
I am a girl without a god.
I am a girl without a devil.
I am a girl without a world.

I am a girl without a universe.
I am a girl without anything.
I am a girl.
I am nothing.

poems.title: Bricklayer's Daughter
poems.text:
I am not your daughter.
I am not your wife.
I am not your mother.
I am not your sister.

I am a stranger.
I am a stranger.
I am a stranger.
I am a stranger.

poems.title: Metamorphosis of Cat into Sun
poems.text:
I am not your cat.
I am not your pet.
I am not your animal.
I am not your possession.

I am a wild thing.
I am a free thing.
I am a bright thing.
I am a fierce thing.

I am a cat become the sun.
I am a cat become the sun.
I am a cat become the sun.

poems.title: You're
poems.text:
You're clown-like, happiest on your knees,
Your fat, shiny paws
Are a good thing.

You're not afraid of anything.
You're not afraid of the dark.
You're not afraid of the night.
You're not afraid of anything.

You're a clown.
You're a clown.
You're a clown.
You're a clown.

But you're also my child.
You're also my child.
You're also my child.
You're also my child.
